issues.failure_explanation: No global area, component-count, curvature, or local-time integrability restriction is imposed. In dimension one, a single allowed regular zero set can contain N_n=ceil(exp(n^3)) distinct points in each interval [n,n+1], with no finite accumulation point and a C^2 defining function having unit derivative magnitude at every zero. For Brownian X started at zero, its surface local time is the sum of the point local times. Each point in [n,n+1] has expected local time bounded below by a positive constant times exp(−C n^2), so the sum has infinite expectation. Constant barriers satisfy all the barrier assumptions in this example.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add global geometric or explicit integrability assumptions ensuring finite expected surface local times. Alternatively replace the unweighted bounds by justified finite expected variation bounds for the actual weighted interface terms.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform surface-local-time input used to obtain the absolute-error rate is false for the admitted noncompact C^2 geometry, even with deterministic initial data and constant diffusion.
issues.title: Finite expected surface local time is not implied by the stated geometry
issues.why_classification: A genuine global geometry/integrability restriction or a contained replacement estimate is required, while common financial hyperplanes and the same error-analysis structure can remain covered.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses do not require distinct interfaces to have local-time-negligible overlaps, but the formula sums the full jump of p over every listed surface. For example, let Γ_1={y=0}, Γ_2={y=h(x)}, where h is smooth, zero for x≤0 and positive for x>0, and take p=|y|+|y−h(x)|. Both surfaces are genuine singular interfaces. On x<0, p=2|y| and its normal-derivative jump is 4 on each listed surface. The proposed sum therefore gives twice the actual local-time contribution there. This problem persists with bounded derivatives and finite expected local times.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Count each geometric interface only once through a suitable partition or multiplicity correction and justify the resulting formula, or impose and verify an overlap condition making pairwise overlaps negligible for the surface local times.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed change-of-variable decomposition, and consequently its use in the absolute-error proof, is not established for the advertised arbitrary finite unions of hypersurfaces.
issues.title: The surface Itô formula double-counts overlapping interfaces
issues.why_classification: Repair requires a contained interface construction or a substantive geometric restriction, rather than an algebraic edit; comparable nonsmooth-barrier coverage can survive.
